name: tensor-viewer
description: View NPY, NPZ, Safetensors and GGUF files: shapes, dtypes, stats and heatmaps. Offline.

tensorViewer.sampleValues.description: Most values read from one tensor for stats, the histogram and the heatmap. Larger tensors are sampled by whole rows spread evenly over the tensor.

tensorViewer.maxRemoteFileMB.description: Files that are not on local disk (remote or virtual workspaces) are read whole. Bigger files show a message instead.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Tensor Viewer
walkthroughs.description: Open NumPy, Safetensors and GGUF files and see what is inside.

steps.title: Open a tensor file
steps.description:
Click any .npy, .npz, .safetensors or .gguf file in the Explorer. It opens in Tensor Viewer with the header read and every tensor listed.
[Find a model file](command:workbench.action.quickOpen?%5B%22.safetensors%22%5D)

media.altText: A GGUF model open in Tensor Viewer with its metadata, tensor table and a heatmap.

steps.title: Inspect one tensor
steps.description: Click a row to see min, max, mean, std, NaN and Inf counts, a histogram, and a heatmap, line plot or image. Use the buttons to copy the shape as a Python tuple or torch.Size.

steps.title: Tune the sample size
steps.description:
Big tensors are sampled by whole rows. Raise the sample size for exact stats on larger tensors.
[Open settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22tensorViewer%22%5D)

scripts.package: npm run build && npx -y @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies -o dist/
